newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Leave bloc standing.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Leave bloc standing.

text.p: Australian bonds made another strong outperformance against the dollar bloc as the local short-end was still offering value after last week's rate cut, which dragged down longer dated yields.

The market once again outpaced Canada which remains under a cloud from the threat of a tightening by the U.S. Federal Reserve when policy makers meet in July, but also from political uncertainty ahead of next week's Canadian election.
Offshore selling was evident of Canadian securities on Wednesday when the usual linchpin of U.S. Treasuries ended a choppy session flat.
The local market was underpinned by an unexpected fall in first quarter business inventories, which is expected to make a large detraction from next week's full GDP.

U.S. Treasuries succumbed to a whippy session on Wednesday, finding some support from April U.S. durable goods orders which came in close to expectations, rising 1.4 percent, although the March data was also revised up to a 2.2 percent negative.
However, the result of the two-year note sale was described as mediocre and saw the market slip back from the highs.

The U.S. faces further supply later on Thursday with the sale of US$12.0 billion of five-year notes, along with data on the latest weekly jobless claims and the May New York National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) Index. The full NAPM is due next Monday.
